newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Profit-taking shaves Singapore shares but trend up.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking shaves Singapore shares but trend up.

text.p: Singapore's key share index slipped back on Tuesday morning as some investors took profits after two days of strong rises, but dealers said the overall trend was still firm.

"Volume is remarkably high -- around 100 million shares in the first hour -- and overseas demand shows no sign of easing yet," said one dealer. "I think the upward momentum is still there for higher numbers."
By 0230 GMT, the benchmark 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 7.77 points lower at 2,264.11 with 121.2 million shares traded. Losers led gainers by 149 to 129.

The most active share was property group Wing Tai Holdings, which saw 5.4 million shares change hands as the stock dropped 12 cents to Singapore $4.48. Dealers said the pullback was mainly profit-taking after the stock jumped 34 cents on Monday.
It was a similar story for several of the banks and industrial companies, which eased down after healthy gains.
The biggest gainer was Singapore Press foreign, which rose 60 cents to S$28.60. Dealers said the stock was being recommended by some local brokers.
